newsitem.title: FRANCE: Continental Express orders 25 Embraer jets.
newsitem.headline: Continental Express orders 25 Embraer jets.

text.p: U.S. airline Continental Express and Brazilian aircraft maker Embraer said on Wednesday that the domestic carrier is buying 25 Embraer regional jets, worth around $350 million.

Continental Express was converting 25 options for Embraer-145 aircraft, announced last September at Britain's Farnborough air show, into firm orders, an Embraer spokesman told Reuters. Speaking at the Paris air show, he said the average price for the EMB-145 was $15 million per plane.

Continental Express, a subsidiary of Continental Airlines, initially announced firm orders for 25 EMB-145 planes and options for 175 more. Wednesday's conversion into orders left 150 options outstanding, the spokesman said.
The latest order is for a longer-range version of the 50-seater EMB-145 which will be powered by twin Allison AE3007A1 turbofan engines, Embraer said in a statement.
Allison, a U.S. subsidiary of British aero-engine maker Rolls Royce Plc, said the order was worth more than $100 million.

Continental Expresses's options were exercisable over the next 12 years, the airline said in separate statement. Continental was the launch customer for the EMB-145 and has received eight aircraft since it took a first delivery last December.

Houston-based Continental Express is using the EMB-145, branded as the ExpressJet, to fly from its Cleveland and Newark hubs. It planned to start flights from Houston this September, Continental Express said.

The Continental Express purchase, notable amid the slow pace of order announcements so far at the air show, follows Tuesday's orders and options for up to 67 Embraer planes from AMR Corp's domestic carrier American Eagle.
American Eagle said it was buying 42 of Embraer's EMB-145 and taking options on a further 25 aircraft. The firm orders alone are worth $700 million.
